units: <cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Berakhot 9:1:18">Y. Ber. IX, 13ᵃ</cite> bot. <he>בא ועמד לו על פתחו של פַּטְרוֹנוֹ וכ׳</he> he comes and stands at the gate of his patron and calls for his slave &c. Ib. 13ᵇ top <he>ב״וד יש לו פ׳ שולט וכ׳</he> (not <he>מלך ב״וד</he>) a human being has a patron who may have power in one province &c.; <cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Avodah Zarah 3:1:18">Y. Ab. Zar. III, 42ᶜ</cite> bot. <cite ref="Q00563"><he>פטרין</he></cite> (corr. acc.). Tanḥ. Vayesheb 8 <he>אתה הוא בטחוני אתה הוא פַטְרוֹנִי</he> thou (God) art my trust, thou art my patron; a. fr.—Pl. <he>פַּטְרוֹנִין</he>, <he>פַּטְרוֹנוֹת</he>.

<cite ref="Shemot Rabbah 14:3">Ex. R. s. 14</cite> <he>שהיו פושעים … שהיו להם פ׳ וכ׳</he> there were sinners in Israel who had Egyptian patrons and lived in affluence and honor, and were unwilling to leave.

<cite ref="Shir HaShirim Rabbah 5:9:1">Cant. R. to V, 9</cite> <he>מה דודך מדוד</he> … <he>מה פטרון הוא מפ׳</he> ‘what is thy friend more than any other friend’, what god is he to be different from any other god, what patron to be different from other patrons? Esth. R. introd. <he>אתם יש לכם פ׳ ומה הן וכ׳</he> you have patrons, and who are they? These are the words of the covenant (<cite ref="Deuteronomy 28:69">Deut. XXVIII, 69</cite>).
<cite ref="Bereishit Rabbah 50:12">Gen. R. s. 50</cite>, end <he>למדינה שהיו לה שני פ׳ וכ׳</he> (not <he>פיט׳</he>) like a province that had two patrons, one a provincial &c.; a. e.
